name: MEATSPACE: AR Urban Domination
description: A persistent AR territory game played across all of GLMZ's physical districts, where player factions claim real intersections, transit nodes, and buildings as digital sovereign zones — defended through physical presence, timed challenges, and BCI-linked reflex duels. The game's map is a live overlay on the city itself, and high-value nodes like the Gray Zone's transit hubs or Tier 3 market plazas become genuine flashpoints where player conflict bleeds into real-world confrontation. Twelve distinct factions have developed their own subcultures, hand signs, and territorial songs.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 player casually captures a the Gray Zone node as a daily challenge, not realizing it's the junction a the Gray Zone faction uses to coordinate food distribution — and they've just made dangerous enemies.
A corponation is quietly buying real estate in MEATSPACE's highest-traffic nodes, and the in-game territory map is starting to predict their acquisitions before they're announced.
The game's anonymous original developer resurfaces to release a 'true version' of MEATSPACE that strips out the Transit Authority's surveillance backdoors — and disappears again immediately after.
